title: Canonical comparison data for simplicial derived-colimit computations
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and a category-colimit bar system $B$ [def-trf-derived-colimit-bar-system]. For any small category $\mathcal E$, ring $R$, and simplicial object $Q$ of $\mathcal E^{op}$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], call $Q$ a resolution when every simplicial set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E^{op}}(T,Q_\bullet)$ is homotopy equivalent to a singleton (allowing finite zigzags of cylinder homotopies). Define $s_Q(F)$ for $F:\mathcal E^{op}\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ by alternating faces in nonpositive cochain degrees, extending by zero in positive degrees. Define $\mathbf H(F)=B_{\mathcal E,R}.L(F[0])$ in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and its semilinear reindexing maps by the bar-system maps and their scalar-restriction localization identifications. Comparison data consist, simultaneously for all these objects, of isomorphisms $a_{Q,F}:s_Q(F)\cong\mathbf H(F)$ for resolutions $Q$, and the following specifications. Each $F$ has a bounded-above projective resolution $P\to F[0]$. For every such resolution the comparison is the roof from the total double complex $P^p(Q_q)$: the evaluation map is the resolution augmentation on the $p=0$ edge and zero off that edge, while the colimit map is the colimit cocone on the $q=0$ edge and zero off that edge; both are quasi-isomorphisms. The comparison composed with the derived resolution comparison equals the inverse evaluation map followed by the colimit map. The bar coordinates are first-vertex coordinates, obtained from the opposite-category coordinates by the sign $(-1)^{n(n+1)/2}$, with their alternating differential and semilinear generator formulas. For every functor $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$, ring map $\rho:R\to S$, natural map $t:F\to\operatorname{Res}_\rho(G\circ u^{op})$, and simplicial map $k:uQ\to Q'$, supply the evaluation chain map whose degree $-n$ sends $x$ to $G(k_n)(t(x))$. When $Q,Q'$ are resolutions its localized map commutes with $a_{Q,F},a_{Q',G}$ and the bar reindexing map, with degreewise scalar restriction. These derived maps preserve identities and composition under the canonical restriction identifications. No resolution condition is imposed on the intermediate $uQ$. This defines the data and their coherence conditions, without asserting that such data exist.
